title: Anthopic's S1 Just Saved The AI Trade - What You Need To Know
creator: Daniel Pronk
summary: Daniel Pronk walks through Anthropic's newly released S-1 filing and argues it has reversed the recent AI sell-off, with AI names spiking again while hyperscalers sell off. He traces revenue from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024, $4.6 billion in 2025 and $16.3 billion year to date in 2026, calling the growth unprecedented, and stresses the headline $80.7 billion net loss is dominated by a $72.4 billion non-cash fair-value loss on convertible shares. On his reading the business is near break-even operationally: adjusted operating margin reached 19% in Q2, operating cash flow was positive $3.9 billion year to date, free cash flow was $3.5 billion on a GAAP basis, and the balance sheet holds $112.4 billion of cash plus $19.3 billion of short-term investments against only $7.2 billion of current liabilities. Consumption-based revenue is 80% of the total, customers over $100,000 of annual spend rose 8x year over year to 11,900, and compute efficiency improved 5.2x. He cites customer examples including AIG, Bristol Myers, DoorDash and Mercado Libre, plus his own use of Muse for his channel. Against that he flags a mooted $1.5 to 2 trillion IPO valuation at 30 to 40 times annualised revenue and roughly $800 billion of future spending commitments. Calls: none recorded — he explicitly says he is not looking to invest in Anthropic or buy its IPO, and Anthropic has no public ticker yet; Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Broadcom appear only as commitment counterparties, with no direction stated for them. Captions garble Anthropic as 'Anthopic' in the title.
